newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume plunges, prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume plunges, prices mixed.

text.p: Istanbul gold exchange volume plunged to 683 kilos on Wednesday, from 2,182 kilos on Friday, the last day of trade before the public holiday marking the end of the Moslem holy month of Ramadan.

"There was quite a lot of physical demand in the morning with the end of the holiday and gold's dollar price falling in world markets. In the afternoon, traders became unwilling to take positions because of uncertainty over market direction," one dealer said.
The morning session saw 663 kilos traded compared to only 20 kilos in the afternoon.
Gold closed at $338.00 an ounce from $340.70 on Friday, but rose in lira terms to 1,301,000 versus the previous 1,299,500 as the lira weakened against the dollar.
The Turkish currency eased to 119,725 to the dollar compared to Friday's 117,760.
Of the day's trade, 90.5 percent was conducted in lira terms.
